# Entity-relationship diagram: woredas-portal (as built from migrations)

Audit 2026-09-24 · generated by `audit-database` · source of truth: `supabase/migrations/*.sql` (90 files) and `src/integrations/supabase/types.ts`

**Scope and method.** This ERD was generated by `raw/audit-database-erd.py` from the migration files, replaying `CREATE TABLE`, `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` and `ADD CONSTRAINT ... PRIMARY KEY / FOREIGN KEY`, and from the `public.Tables` section of `types.ts`. The two agree exactly: 66 tables and 17 views, with no column-level drift (`raw/audit-database-column-drift.json`). The live database was **not** reachable, so any difference between the live DB and the migrations is unverified. Run Appendix C queries 1-4 to confirm.

**Legend.**
- Only key columns are drawn so that 66 entities stay readable: PK, FK, `woreda_id`, `status`, and every sensitive column. The full column list for each table is in `raw/audit-database-table-ddl.sql` and `types.ts`.
- `PK` / `FK` are taken from the constraints in the migrations. 190 FKs were extracted (`raw/audit-database-fks.json`). The 189 relationships drawn here leave out `app_user.user_id -> auth.users`.
- Sensitive columns carry an attribute comment `"SENSITIVE: <class>"` and are also listed as `%% SENSITIVE` lines at the top of the diagram. There are 53 in total.
- `(enc copy)` means that a `*_enc` pgp_sym ciphertext column exists **alongside** a plaintext column that is still authoritative (see WP-DB-005).

**Tenant model.** Every tenant table carries `woreda_id -> woreda.woreda_id` (54 FKs reference `woreda`). Exceptions:
- Platform tables with no `woreda_id`: `console_role`, `console_role_permission`, `id_card_template`, `id_card_template_field`, `id_card_template_field_draft`, `workflow_transition` and `rate_limit_bucket`.
- Child tables scoped through their parent: `credential_request_status_history`, `credential_status_history`, `service_request_status_history` and `tenant_role_permission`.
- `woreda_id` is nullable by design on `app_user` (super admins), `audit_log` (platform events) and `credential_verification_log` (probes that matched nothing).

No FK is composite `(woreda_id, id)`. Tenant consistency across FKs is enforced only by triggers, and only on some tables (WP-DB-012).

**Structural observations.**
- There are no `DEFERRABLE` constraints. The resident/household cycle (`resident.current_household_id -> household`, `household.household_head_resident_id / spouse_resident_id / alternate_head_resident_id -> resident`) works only because both sides are nullable.
- `id_card_template_field` and `id_card_template_field_draft` have no FK to `id_card_template(template_type)`, so orphan rows are possible.
- `workflow_transition` and `rate_limit_bucket` have no FKs, by design.
- Counters are ordinary tables (`*_sequence`, incremented with `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... RETURNING`), not Postgres sequences. There is no `CREATE SEQUENCE` in any migration.
- `ON DELETE CASCADE` from `woreda` to its children means that deleting a tenant (super_admin only) removes kebele, settings, role_permission, office and similar rows. `service_request` cascades to its status history and attachments.

## Views (not drawn)

All 17 views are `security_invoker = true` at their latest definition:

- `approval_queue_v` and `household_member_roster`
- 15 `*_decrypted` views that project `decrypt_pii_*()` over their base table: `resident`, `household`, `service_request`, `payment`, `rental_occupancy`, `rental_occupancy_request`, `rent_charge`, `rent_rate_history`, `rent_payment_settlement`, `payment_reconciliation_exception`, `arrears_repayment_plan`, `arrears_repayment_installment`, `arrears_installment_charge`, `rent_reminder` and `service_request_checkpoint`.

## Reconciliation with `docs/erd.md` (added by audit-architecture)

This section compares the as-built ERD above (66 tables and 17 views, reconstructed from all 90 migrations) with the project's own `docs/erd.md`, last changed in commit `eb3d283` on 2026-09-14. Nothing above this section was rewritten.

| Item | `docs/erd.md` says | As built (migrations) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Table count | "52 tables", live-enumerated with "zero drift" (`docs/erd.md:10-12`) | 66 tables (`raw/audit-database-catalog.json`) | **Stale.** The 52 was plausibly true on 2026-09-14. The 14 tables added since are all in migrations 71–89, committed from 2026-09-21. 66 − 14 = 52, so the earlier count and the migrations agree. |
| Rental financial core | Not documented | `rent_account`, `rent_account_sequence`, `rent_charge`, `rent_rate_history`, `rent_reminder`, `rent_payment_settlement`, `rental_payment`, `rental_policy`, `arrears_repayment_plan`, `arrears_repayment_installment`, `arrears_installment_charge`, `arrears_plan_sequence`, `payment_reconciliation_exception` (migrations `00000000000071`–`00000000000089`) | **Missing from docs.** None of the 13 names appear anywhere in `docs/erd.md`. |
| `service_request_checkpoint` | Not documented | Created by `00000000000083_rental_phase5_checkpoint.sql:29` | **Missing from docs.** |
| Views | `approval_queue_v` and the Phase C `*_decrypted` views described in prose (`docs/erd.md:31-40`, `:600`) | 17 views. 15 of them are not named in `docs/erd.md`, including every `*_decrypted` view and the 10 rental and arrears decrypted views | **Incomplete.** |
| Encrypted companion columns | Eight columns listed (`docs/erd.md:31-35`) | That list plus `resident.national_id_no_enc` (`00000000000044`) and the rental and arrears monetary `_enc` columns | **Stale.** The statement that the plaintext stays authoritative is still true (WP-DB-005). |
| Tenant model | Every tenant table carries `woreda_id`; `workflow_transition` is platform-level | Confirmed: 54 FKs to `woreda`; 7 platform tables; 4 parent-scoped child tables; 3 nullable `woreda_id` columns | **Confirmed.** |
| Cross-tenant FK consistency | Not discussed | No composite `(woreda_id, id)` FK exists; consistency is trigger-enforced on some tables only | **Not documented** (WP-DB-012). |
| Counters | Described under "Sequence / counter tables" (`docs/erd.md:609`) | Ordinary tables incremented with `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`, with no `CREATE SEQUENCE`. Two rental counters are not listed | **Stale.** Tenant write access to the counters is WP-DB-006. |

**Orphans and unwritten stores.** No table is orphaned in the FK sense apart from the three documented exceptions: the template field tables with no FK to `id_card_template`, `workflow_transition` and `rate_limit_bucket`. Some tables have no application writer:

- `approval` has no client writer and no RPC writer.
- `household_location` has no client use.
- `rental_payment` and `rent_reminder` are written only inside DEFINER RPCs.
- `office` is seeded by a trigger.

These are recorded in `system-architecture.md` §5 so that "no undocumented stores" (INSA A-02) is satisfied explicitly.

**Live state.** Whether production has all 66 tables depends on the 14 rental and checkpoint tables having been applied. The migration ledger cannot show this (WP-OPS-007). Appendix C query 1 in `reference/appendix-c-catalog-queries.md` settles it. Until then, INSA A-07's "ERD matches live schema" stays **UNVERIFIED** for the live half.
